newsitem.title: USA: U.S. "commends" report of French snub to Christopher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. "commends" report of French snub to Christopher.

text.p: The State Department on Thursday commended a newspaper report that said Secretary of State Warren Christopher had been snubbed by French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette during a NATO meeting.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns described the article, by the Washington Post's correspondent William Drozdiak, as "a very fine report" and said it contained only one inaccuracy, the timing of the incident.
His comments appeared to add oil to the flames of a transatlantic controversy that soured Christopher's last trip before he retires and hands over to U.N. ambassador Madeleine Albright.

Both NATO and the French government have denied that de Charette snubbed Christopher by walking out of a toast in his honour by NATO Secretary General Javier Solana at an alliance lunch on Wednesday, as the newspaper reported.

Calling Drozdiak "an excellent journalist," Burns told a State Department briefing: "There was only one slight factual inaccuracy in that story ... the tribute by Secretary Solana did not occur at lunch. The tribute occurred at the end of the day at the NATO hall."
"I would commend that article to you," he added.

The Washington Post quoted an unnamed senior U.S. official as saying: "It was an incredible display of petulant behaviour. Everybody knows there are tensions in the French-American relationship, but nobody expects them to be shown at a personal level."
De Charette called the report a "manipulation" and his spokesman, Jacques Rummelhardt, branded it an "ill-intentioned lie" aimed at damaging already frayed ties between Paris and Washington.
The French minister told Reuters: "I cannot explain it. But I severely condemn this kind of manoeuvring because I do not doubt this was a manipulation."

The controversy reflects the raw state of Franco-U.S. relations, affected by disputes over the reform of NATO's military structure, the succession to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, France's drive for a bigger say in the Middle East and Western policy on Zaire.
Probably the most serious fight concerns the future of NATO's southern command, which controls the Mediterranean.
France demands that Washington hand over the post it has held since NATO was created in 1949 to a European. The United States has refused and is not amenable to compromise.
